### Summary

Every boundary callback is a function of a tensor, a dimension and a `BoundaryFuncOptions` context, entered
into one global registry under its name by the `BC_FUNCTION` macro ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}}),
which also declares the contract a callback must keep: it may be called again on a thin tangential ghost slab
after an exchange, so it must not depend on the orthogonal extent of its input and a second call must
reproduce the first. The card names a callback per face; `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` appends `_inner`
or `_outer`, looks the name up in the registry, and refuses a name that is not there. Construction of the block
then nulls the callbacks of the faces that another block or a periodic wrap supplies, so that "physical face"
and "callback present" mean the same thing from then on.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Classify and dispatch each block face.

**Data.** Six face names map to callbacks; no physical units.

**Placement.** Parse names, then remove layout-owned callbacks at construction.

**Activation.** Inside `boundary-condition/external`, a face without a key defaults to `reflecting`; a deck without
that block installs no callback, and the block then refuses to build.

**Guarantee / limits.** Physical-face and diffusion-wall predicates differ.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

This is dispatch infrastructure, so there is no differential equation to discretize. Two predicates carry the
chapter. A face is *physical* exactly when its callback is non-null: `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_physical_boundary`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_physical_boundary >}}) tests the entry of
`bfuncs` at the face index that `face_of` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp face_of >}}) returns, first
match winning in x3, x2, x1 order. A face is a *diffusion wall* when it is physical and its recorded name is one
of `reflecting_inner`, `reflecting_outer`, `fixed_temperature_inner` or `fixed_temperature_outer`:
`MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}})
is a whitelist, and a physical face whose name was not recorded (a callback installed programmatically without
a name) warns once and is not a wall.

Both predicates read one classification. `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::face_kind`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::face_kind >}}) gives a face with a callback one
`FaceKind` ({{< code src/layout/exchange.hpp FaceKind >}}): `periodic` for a name starting with `periodic`, `wall`
for the four whitelisted names, `outflow` for the outflow callback, and `custom` for everything else, including an
unnamed callback. A face without a callback is `interior`, and `Exchange::kind`
({{< code src/layout/exchange.cpp Exchange::kind >}}) then refines it from the layout into `seam_x1`, `panel`,
`periodic` or `interior`. The hydro predicate `HydroImpl::is_x1_wall`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::is_x1_wall >}}) is a third set: an x1 face of kind `wall`, `outflow` or
`custom`. The sets are nested but not equal: an outflow face is physical and an x1 wall for the hydro, but not a
diffusion wall; an in-block periodic x1 face (slab layout) is physical but neither kind of wall.

A repeated fill must reproduce the same ghost values from the owned slab. This idempotence is a contract on the
callback, not a property of every tensor map; the registry asks for it because the corner refresh of
@sec-ch14-timing calls the x1 callbacks a second time on a slab that is only $n_g$[^rg-88a9e0a977ff] cells wide in the
tangential direction. Check C1 exercises the contract for the built-in mirror and copy rules; no spatial order
is assigned to dispatch [check `src/snapy_report/ch14/checks/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch14/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The face order is x1 inner, x1 outer, x2 inner, x2 outer, x3 inner, x3 outer (`BoundaryFace`,
{{< code src/bc/bc.hpp BoundaryFace >}}); in the four-dimensional hydro tensor `(variable, x3, x2, x1)` these
faces act on dimensions 3, 2 and 1, and a callback receives the dimension it fills. The context
`BoundaryFuncOptions` ({{< code src/bc/bc.hpp BoundaryFuncOptions >}}) carries a non-owning EOS[^rg-b6eeb6bec592] and coordinate
pointer, the saved backgrounds that outflow needs, the representation (`kConserved`, `kPrimitive` or
`kScalar`) and the ghost width $n_g$. On a collapsed direction (one cell) the card entry is not read: the
parser pushes a null callback and an empty name for both faces of that direction whenever a later direction
has more than one cell, so the face indices of the other directions stay in place.

`MeshBlockImpl::reset` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}) nulls, for a slab or cubed
layout, the callback of every face that has a neighbouring block in that direction or whose direction is
periodic in the layout; the cubed-sphere layout keeps its own panel rules and is not touched by this step. A
non-null custom callback therefore still counts as physical for every predicate above. No accuracy order
follows from classification.

### Code

**How to use.** Use this fragment in a complete deck with an active x1 direction. Names omit the `_inner` and
`_outer` suffixes; the parser adds them. A layout-owned face loses its callback after construction.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `boundary-condition`[^rg-01888ad64fad], `x1-inner`[^rg-7cca0798643a], `x1-outer`[^rg-ffc56ec72f7b].
```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: reflecting
    x1-outer: reflecting
```

A horizontally periodic domain with a solid wall at the bottom names `reflecting` on `x1-inner` (the wall; also the
default) and `periodic` on both faces of each horizontal direction, `x2-inner`[^rg-1526e082e385] and `x2-outer`[^rg-1d8fc442205c], and on a 3-D grid
`x3-inner`[^rg-2baf9e7ccdf4] and `x3-outer`[^rg-c1524ff083b4], as in {{< code examples/earth_crm.yaml >}}; a periodic direction needs the name on both
of its faces (@sec-ch14-periodic), and $x_1$[^rg-e4c312927e59] is the vertical (@sec-appa-conventions).

**Refusals and prerequisites.** An unregistered name such as `typo` is refused as "Boundary function 'typo_inner'
is not defined." Unknown map keys are rejected by `check_keys`; a collapsed direction does not read its face names.

**Read the implementation.** `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` reads every face name in one loop over `side`
([`src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp:114-126`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L114-L126)), verbatim at the pin:

```cpp
    for (std::string side : {"inner", "outer"}) {
      auto key = "x" + std::to_string(d + 1) + "-" + side;
      auto name = external_bc[key].as<std::string>("reflecting");
      if (name == "periodic") {
        if (d == 0 && op->layout()->type() == "cubed")
          op->layout()->periodic_z(true);
        if (d == 1) op->layout()->periodic_x(true);
        if (d == 2) op->layout()->periodic_y(true);
      }
      name += "_" + side;
      TORCH_CHECK(get_bc_func().find(name) != get_bc_func().end(),
                  "Boundary function '", name, "' is not defined.");
      op->bfuncs().push_back(get_bc_func()[name]);
```

The default `reflecting` applies only inside a present `boundary-condition/external` block: a deck without the
`boundary-condition` block, or without its `external` map, returns before this loop, installs no callback, and
`MeshBlockImpl` then stops with "bfuncs size must be at least" for every active direction
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::MeshBlockImpl >}}). Within the block, the default `reflecting` supplies the
face name, the suffix names the registry entry, and the lookup refuses a name
that is not registered: the dispatch contract of the Derivation layer.

| context | {{< code src/bc/bc.hpp BoundaryFuncOptions >}} | `BoundaryFuncOptions` | none |
| faces | {{< code src/bc/bc.hpp BoundaryFace >}} | `BoundaryFace` | none |

: Implementation sites for registry. {#tbl-ch14-registry-code}

1. Validate the keys under `boundary-condition` and `boundary-condition/external`, read each face name with
   the default `reflecting`, append `_inner` or `_outer`, and reject a name absent from the registry. A
   periodic x2 or x3 name sets `periodic_x` or `periodic_y`; a periodic x1 name sets `periodic_z` only when
   the layout type is `cubed`. The anchor `periodic_z` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}.
2. At construction, null the callbacks of the faces the layout owns. The anchor `bfuncs` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}.
3. Classify at the consuming operator: `is_physical_boundary` for the hydro, the exchange and the implicit
   solve; `is_wall_boundary` for diffusion, where an unnamed callback warns once and returns false. The anchor
   `is_wall_boundary` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}}.

|---|---|---|---|
| `test_yaml_keys.release` | An unknown key under `boundary-condition` or `boundary-condition/external` is refused with its path in the message | exact string containment | test helper `expect_refused` |
| `test_wb_wall_corner.release` | A stock reflecting wall and a user-installed wall both keep a resting column at rest | Mach at most $10^{-12}$ | test constant |

: Source-test assertions and report-only checks for registry. {#tbl-ch14-registry-tests}

The refusal helper is `expect_refused` ({{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp expect_refused overload=1 >}},
{{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp expect_refused overload=2 >}}); the boundary cases are
{{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp yaml_keys.boundary_condition_refuses_an_unknown_key >}} and
{{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp yaml_keys.external_boundaries_refuse_an_unknown_key >}}.

The rest assertions are `EXPECT_LE` on the Mach number in
{{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.x2_uniform_rest_keeps_u2_zero >}} and
{{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.user_wall_keeps_u2_zero >}}.

**Not provided:** a round-off derivation for each tolerance, because the cited tests give acceptance
criteria without deriving each round-off bound, and this book does not derive those bounds.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch16-ch11.

The report-only checks `[C1]` establish that copy, parity, idempotence and corner ownership hold
exactly.[^ch11-registry-run]
These checks exercise report formulas, not the compiled boundary kernels. The source-test table records
assertions and tolerances, not new CPU[^rg-0ab3aad6818c], CUDA[^rg-7d5758f753ba] or multi-rank solver results.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The fixed-temperature names are accepted by the diffusion whitelist, but the boundary sources at the pin
register no callback under them, so the card cannot select a thermal wall. The comment above the whitelist
describes the outflow ghost as a zero-gradient statement, while the outflow callback of @sec-ch14-outflow
builds a characteristic state; the classification itself (not a wall) is unaffected. A cubed-sphere panel
face that carries a custom callback counts as physical wherever a physical-face test is used.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
